q: If green hydrogen or ammonia is shipped from Duqm to the EU, what does CBAM count?
title: Duqm hydrogen and ammonia under CBAM
short: Hydrogen counts direct emissions only, close to zero for electrolysis. Ammonia is a fertiliser good, so indirect emissions from electricity count too; renewable power with proper evidence keeps that low. Projects at Duqm are still in development, so check each project's status.
audience: Hydrogen and ammonia project developers in Oman and their EU offtakers

p: Under CBAM, hydrogen carries direct emissions only. Electrolysis emits almost nothing directly; the electricity behind it is not counted for hydrogen.

ul: Direct emissions from synthesis and any fuel burnt.
Indirect emissions from electricity consumed, which needs evidence of renewable supply to count as low.

p: EU renewable fuel rules for RFNBO status are separate from CBAM and have their own evidence requirements.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for.

sources.label: European Commission, CBAM legislation and guidance
